source.title: Adaptation to visuomotor transformations: consolidation, interference, and forgetting.

confidence_rationale: Direct empirical instantiation of the exact A->B->A assay MECH-476's falsifier proposes, in humans, showing resistance-to-interference grows with BOTH elapsed interval (24 h vs 5 min) AND doubled initial training (dose). This validates the assay and the two levers the falsifier varies; it does not test REE's substrate, so mapping fidelity to REE is design-level not mechanism-level, and it carries a methodological warning (anterograde interference / washout) the REE experiment must honour.
failure_signatures: Without washout blocks removing anterograde interference, a counter-rotation interfered even at a 24 h interval -- i.e. apparent 'no consolidation' can be a retrieval-competition artefact rather than a true absence of a consolidation process. The REE A->B->A design must remove analogous anterograde effects (measure retained A cleanly) or a null result is uninterpretable.

Visuomotor rotation, unlike force-field or sequence learning, did NOT consolidate over time under the naive design -- consolidation is task/representation-specific, so a null in one REE competence-band does not generalise across substrates.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Consolidation is operationally defined as resistance to retrograde interference (interference by task B on the initial learning of task A). Rotation learning becomes resistant to a 5-min counter-rotation both when the interval to B is extended to 24 h (with anterograde effects removed by washout) and when the amount of initial training is doubled.
mapping.ree_translation: The claim MECH-476 adopts this exact operational definition: retention (consolidation) is a PROCESS whose signature is interference-resistance that grows with install DOSE (BC episodes, analogous to doubled training) and A->B INTERVAL (offline steps, analogous to 5 min vs 24 h). SUPPORTED-vs-WEAKENED in REE is decided by whether REE's retained-fraction trajectory shows the same monotone dependence Krakauer measured behaviourally.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a design template, not a mechanism transfer. Krakauer studied human explicit/implicit visuomotor adaptation with declarative and cerebellar components; REE is a BC->RL agent with a value estimator and a KL update-constraint. The prediction that dose and interval matter transfers; the physiological mechanism does not. Critically, Krakauer's own result shows the assay can FALSELY report no-consolidation if anterograde retrieval interference is not washed out -- the REE implementation inherits that confound and must control it, or an invariance result cannot be read as WEAKENED.
mapping.source_context: Healthy adult humans; screen-cursor 30-degree visuomotor rotation adaptation; A->B->A paradigm with counter-rotation as interfering task B; RCT.

confidence_components.notes: Canonical, well-replicated RCT and the literal design source cited in MECH-476's what_would_answer. Source quality weighted heavily. Mapping fidelity high at the design level (the assay is exactly what the falsifier runs), lower at the mechanism level; transfer risk moderate (human motor adaptation -> RL competence retention). Confidence set above the component mean because the paper's load-bearing role here is to license the ASSAY, which it does decisively.
